q: Statements: All nurses in this ward are trained in first aid. Sara is a nurse in this ward. Which conclusion follows?
o: Everyone trained in first aid is a nurse
Sara is not trained in first aid
Sara is trained in first aid
Some nurses in this ward are not trained in first aid
x: Sara belongs to the group 'nurses in this ward', and every member of that group is trained in first aid, so Sara is too. The reverse statement does not follow.

q: Given that no P is Q and every R is Q, which statement must be true?
x: Every R lies inside Q, and no P lies inside Q, so no R can be P. Nothing says every Q is an R, and the statements about some P being R contradict the conclusion.

q: It is known that some X are Y and some Y are Z. Which statement can be concluded with certainty?
x: 'Some X are Y' can be turned round to 'some Y are X'. Two 'some' statements give no definite link between X and Z, and 'some Y are Z' does not mean every Z is Y.

q: Every W is an X, and at least one W is a Y. Which statement must be true?
o: At least one X is a Y
x: The W that is a Y is also an X, because every W is an X; so at least one X is a Y. Nothing is said about Y that are not W, or about X that are not W.

q: Three facts are given: some P are Q, every Q is R, and no R is S. Which statement must be true?
x: The P that are Q are also R, and no R is S, so those P are not S. Other P may or may not be S, so 'No P is S' does not follow; no Q can be S.

q: Bilal is older than Hamza but younger than Ali. Who is the oldest of the three?
x: The order is Ali, then Bilal, then Hamza from oldest to youngest, so Ali is the oldest.

q: Faisal is taller than Usman. Usman is taller than Zain. Asad is shorter than Zain. Kashif is shorter than Usman but taller than Zain. Who is in the middle when the five stand in order of height?
x: From tallest: Faisal, Usman, Kashif, Zain, Asad. The third of five is Kashif.

q: In a class of 35 students ranked by marks with no ties, Ayesha is 10th from the top. Sana is five places below Ayesha. What is Sana's rank from the bottom?
x: Sana is 15th from the top. Rank from the bottom = 35 - 15 + 1 = 21st.

q: Introducing a woman, Bilal said, "Her mother is the wife of my father's father." How is the woman related to Bilal?
x: The wife of Bilal's father's father is Bilal's grandmother. Her daughter is his father's sister, that is, his paternal aunt.

q: Sana is the sister of Imran. Imran is the son of Rehana. Rehana's father is Akbar. How is Sana related to Akbar?
x: Sana is Imran's sister, so she is also Rehana's daughter. Rehana is Akbar's daughter, so Sana is Akbar's granddaughter.

q: Saad is the only son of Kamal. Hira is Kamal's daughter. Nazia is Saad's wife, and Ahmed is the son of Saad and Nazia. How is Hira related to Ahmed?
x: Hira and Saad are both Kamal's children, so Hira is Saad's sister. Saad is Ahmed's father, so Hira is Ahmed's father's sister, his paternal aunt.

q: Zara is facing east. She turns to her left. Which direction is she facing now?
x: A left turn is 90 degrees anticlockwise; from east this brings her to face north.

q: From the school gate, Kashif cycles 7 km due east. He then turns left for 5 km, turns left again for 7 km, and finally turns right for 3 km. How far is he from the gate, and in which direction?
x: East 7 and later west 7 cancel out. He walks north 5 km and then, after the right turn from facing west, north 3 km more: 8 km north.

q: Nida is facing north-west. She turns 135 degrees clockwise. Which direction is she facing now?
x: Clockwise from north-west: 45 degrees brings her to north, and another 90 degrees to east.

q: Usman walks 2 km west, turns left and walks 5 km, then turns left again and walks 14 km. Where is he now from his starting point?
x: Left from west is south (5 km), left from south is east (14 km). He ends 12 km east and 5 km south of the start; the distance is the square root of 144 + 25 = 13 km, towards the south-east.

q: Four books, red, green, blue and yellow, stand in a row on a shelf. The red book is at the left end. The green book is immediately to the right of the red book. The blue book is not at the right end. Which book is at the right end?
x: Red and green take the first two places. Blue cannot be last, so blue is third and yellow is at the right end.

q: Hina, Iqra, Javeria, Kiran, Laiba and Mehwish sit in a row facing north. Kiran is at the right end. Hina is second from the left, and Laiba sits immediately to Hina's right. Mehwish sits next to Kiran. Javeria is not at an end. Who sits immediately to the left of Mehwish?
x: Seats from the left: Hina 2, Laiba 3, Kiran 6, and Mehwish 5 (next to Kiran). Javeria cannot be at an end, so she takes seat 4 and Iqra seat 1. Seat 4, Javeria, is left of Mehwish.

q: A building has six floors numbered 1 (lowest) to 6. Rafay, Sadia, Tariq, Umer, Vania and Wajid each live on a different floor. Rafay lives on floor 4. Sadia lives two floors above Rafay, and Tariq directly below Rafay. Umer lives on an odd-numbered floor below Tariq. Wajid does not live next to Sadia. Who lives on floor 5?
x: Rafay 4, Sadia 6, Tariq 3, and Umer 1 (the only odd floor below 3). Floors 2 and 5 are left; Wajid cannot be next to Sadia, so he is on 2 and Vania on 5.

q: Six exams, Biology, Chemistry, English, Logic, Physics and Urdu, are held one per day from Monday to Saturday. Chemistry is on Thursday. Physics is two days before Chemistry, and Biology the day after Physics. English is not on Monday. Urdu is after Chemistry. Which exam is on Monday?
x: Physics is Tuesday and Biology Wednesday. Monday, Friday and Saturday remain; English cannot be Monday and Urdu must be after Thursday, so Logic is on Monday.

q: Adeel, Babar, Danish, Ehsan, Farhan and Gohar sit equally spaced around a round table, facing the centre. Adeel sits opposite Ehsan. Babar sits immediately to Adeel's left. Gohar sits opposite Babar. Danish does not sit next to Ehsan. Who sits opposite Danish?
x: Fixing Adeel, Ehsan, Babar and Gohar leaves two seats: one beside Ehsan and one beside Adeel. Danish must take the seat beside Adeel, and the seat opposite it is Farhan's.

q: Seven people stand in a single queue. Fahad is third from the front. Waleed stands behind Fahad, with exactly two people between them. How many people stand behind Waleed?
x: With two people between them, Waleed is in place 3 + 3 = 6. In a queue of seven, one person stands behind him.

q: Village Q is 4 km north of village P. Village R is 4 km east of village Q. Village S is 4 km south of village R. Where is village S from village P?
x: Going north 4 km and then south 4 km cancels out, leaving only the 4 km east step. So S is 4 km east of P.
